name: color-area-picker
title: Color area picker
description: Any colour, not just swatches: a saturation and brightness area, a hue slider, optional alpha and a typed code, all keyboard operable.
docs: value and onValueChange(value, color) speak the colour as a string in format (hex #2563eb, rgb(37, 99, 235) or hsl(221, 83%, 53%); with alpha the code carries it: eight hex digits, rgba() or hsla()) and as { h, s, v, a } (hue in degrees, saturation and brightness in percent, alpha 0 to 1). value takes a string in any of those formats or the object, and the picker keeps its own hue, so dragging into black, white or grey does not lose it the way a code would. The area is a two-axis slider: arrow keys move 1%, Shift 10%, Home and End go to the left and right edge, Page Up and Page Down to the top and bottom, and its value text reads Saturation 80%, brightness 60%. The hue and opacity sliders are Radix sliders over a rainbow and a quiet checkerboard. The code box accepts #rgb, #rrggbb, #rrggbbaa, rgb() and hsl() whatever the format and says what is wrong in words. The chosen colour is shown beside its code with its contrast against white and black in words (4.6:1, passes AA). swatches is a row of presets (a radio group), inline puts the picker in the page instead of behind a button, and the eye dropper button appears only where the browser has one, inside the code box so the code has the whole row (an rgba() or hsla() code keeps its alpha in view, and on the narrowest phone the colour tile beside the box gives way to it). The button shows the code on one line. id, aria-invalid, aria-describedby, aria-label and aria-labelledby go to the button, or to the area when the picker is inline, so a form label and error can be wired to it. name posts the colour. The colour helpers (parseColor, formatColor, contrastRatio) live in color-area-picker/colors.
